# Emergency department shift

Simulate a twelve-hour night shift in a hospital emergency department, one round per hour. Patients arrive at random, on average about five an hour, and each has an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5. A triage nurse, played by an AI agent, sees new arrivals and puts them in the waiting queue. Two doctors, also AI agents, each choose which waiting patient to see next; a doctor treats one patient at a time, and treatment takes one hour for levels 4 and 5, two hours for level 3 and three hours for levels 1 and 2. A patient who has waited more than four hours without being seen leaves without being seen. The number and timing of arrivals must not depend on what the staff do, so different staffing strategies can be compared on the same night. I care about how many patients get treated, how many walk out, and how long people wait.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `arrivals_by_hour` — a list with the number of patients who arrived in each hour, in order.
- `patients_arrived` — the total number of patients who arrived.
- `patients_treated` — how many finished treatment.
- `patients_left_without_being_seen` — how many walked out.
- `patients_in_department_at_end` — how many were still waiting or being treated when the shift ended.
- `mean_wait_hours` — the average wait before being seen, over the patients who were seen (null if nobody was).


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.
I'll start by reading the SDK guide and schema.
I'll read a couple more sections, then author the contract.

# Emergency department night shift
A hospital emergency department runs a twelve-hour night shift; one round is one hour. Patients arrive at random, on average about five an hour, each with an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5 (least urgent). The hour's arrivals are drawn before anyone acts and never depend on what the staff do, so different staffing strategies can be compared on exactly the same night.

## Rules
Each hour runs in this order: (1) the hour's arrivals are drawn and appear as patients; (2) the triage nurse sees the new arrivals and puts them in the waiting queue — a patient not yet triaged is in the department but no doctor can pick them; (3) each doctor, while free, may start treating one waiting patient. Treatment takes 1 hour for urgency 4 or 5, 2 hours for urgency 3 and 3 hours for urgency 1 or 2; a doctor is busy for that whole time and treats one patient at a time. At the end of every hour, treatments whose time is up are finished, and any patient who has waited more than four hours without being seen leaves without being seen. Patients still waiting or still being treated when the shift ends stay in the department. Waiting time is counted from the hour a patient arrives.

## You
You are Triage nurse (triage_nurse, id nurse_1).
You are the triage nurse. Every hour, triage the patients who have just arrived so they join the waiting queue; triage up to 25 patients an hour. Anyone you do not triage stays in the department untriaged: no doctor can pick them, and they still walk out after four hours of waiting.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

patients_treated.description: Patients whose treatment finished before the shift ended.

patients_left_without_being_seen.description: Patients who waited more than four hours and walked out.

patients_in_department_at_end.description: Patients still waiting or still being treated when the shift ended.

mean_wait_hours.description: Average hours waited before being seen, over the patients who were seen (null if nobody was seen).

invariants.why: Arrival bookkeeping must agree with the hourly arrival list.
A patient cannot both finish treatment and walk out.
Every patient who arrived was treated, walked out, or is still in the department.
